checkpoint_review: The Router's assessment is accurate and appropriately critical. The sign fails the primary geometry checkpoint because it exhibits a physically impossible 'ribbon-like' curvature rather than the rigid planar structure required for a street sign. The text checkpoints are correctly marked as failed due to mirroring and gibberish ('CANEJAK', 'CRUE'). I agree with all Router verdicts, including the failure of the material checkpoint; while the surface texture mimics paint, the structural failure (melting/twisting) negates the functional definition of durable aluminum/plastic construction.
artifact_review: The Router correctly identified severe text gibberish (severity 4) and structural collapse (severity 3). Upon reflection, the structural artifact is indeed the dominant failure mode; the sign appears to be melting or fusing with the post in a way that defies physics entirely. The background perspective distortion (severity 2) is present but secondary. No new artifacts were found by experts, but the combination of total text illegibility and physical impossibility justifies a very low artifact score.
alignment_reasoning: Only 3/9 checkpoints passed (mounting height, contrast, color palette). Critical failures in geometry (non-rigid), text (gibberish/mirrored), and function (navigation impossible) result in a very low alignment score. The object resembles a street sign only superficially through color and general placement, but lacks all defining functional and structural characteristics.
artifact_reasoning: Severe structural collapse (melting/twisting metal) and illegible mirrored text are dominant artifacts. The sign lacks physical rigidity and logical mounting hardware. Background warping is a minor secondary issue. The severity of the structural failure combined with complete text failure warrants a score below 1.0.
